qa.answer: Four options. Hold Sendai while Plzen reserves stock to a 2 Nov decision and book Q1 allocation now (no cost today, recommended), move the whole bar line to Plzen (USD 18K), split it 60/40 between Sendai and Plzen (USD 7.2K), or add a 20 bar Plzen buffer for Q1 jobs (USD 9K). None of them moves a redelivery.

The recommended hold is cheapest at nothing today; if Sendai cannot confirm by 2 Nov, the Plzen fallback costs USD 18K. Of the options that spend money now, the 60/40 split is cheapest at USD 7.2K. Resourcing the other alloy lines barely helps: every approved alternate is slower than Sendai's revised dates except Monongahela on the 6 sheets of Haynes-type 188 on 4500019413-00030, which would land 18 Dec instead of 22 Jan.

In 2024 a US mill cut nickel superalloy allocation by 35% for Q3 (PRE-05). We split 60/40 to a second casting source at an 8% premium for USD 118K and engine inductions held. The lesson was to lock second-source slots in the same week the allocation notice lands, because they sell out within 10 days.

No induction moves. WO-2612 needs 40 Ti-6Al-4V bars at its 18 Nov induction, and Sendai's allocation moves PO 4500018629-00010 to 10 Dec, 22 days late against 30 days of float. The redelivery only moves if Sendai slips more than 8 further days, which the 2 Nov Plzen decision point is set to catch.
